title: Borrowable leases + eviction-fencing for prefix-cohort KV cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As continuous batching increases request concurrency, traditional TTL/LRU eviction interacts poorly with prefix-aware allocations and GPU slab fragmentation. We observed two classes of failures in stress tests: (1) live inference requests reading a key that is reclaimed mid-batch causing incorrect KV hits and model outputs, and (2) non-deterministic latency spikes due to on-path compaction triggered by eviction churn.

Goal: Design and implement a borrowable-lease + eviction-fencing mechanism for the KV cache that preserves correctness under continuous batching, minimizes synchronous compaction on the GPU, and provides deterministic safety invariants suitable for rollout to Dedicated and Hosted fleets.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Borrowable Leases: each KV prefix allocation carries a lease token with an expiry epoch and a borrow flag. Inference workers may 'borrow' a lease for short-lived usage (e.g., current batch or microsecond window) without extending global retention. Borrowing records are lightweight counters in CPU-side metadata and reflected as pinned refs in the runtime's eviction planner.
- Eviction Fences: eviction operations create a fence epoch. A fence marks ranges that cannot be reclaimed until all borrow counts are zero and the fence epoch is older than the global compact watermark. Fences provide an atomic handoff: once a fence is installed for a slab, no new borrows are permitted and existing borrows must drain before eviction proceeds.
- Cohort-based rebalancing: prefixes are grouped into cohorts by sequence-length and RU profile. Eviction decisions operate at cohort granularity to avoid oscillation caused by per-prefix churn and to reduce slab compaction frequency.
- GPU slab soft-compaction: avoid synchronous compaction by scheduling best-effort soft-compaction tasks on idle GPU cycles; only force compaction on high-watermark breach or explicit SLA-critical evictions.
- Correctness invariants: (a) Safety: a borrows-visible key cannot be reclaimed while borrowed (no use-after-free). (b) Liveness: under normal load, eviction will complete within bounded time unless borrow rates continuously saturate (in which case we fall back to admission controls). (c) Determinism: fence epochs and borrow counters produce deterministic decisions given identical event ordering (useful for reproducible regressions and tests).

Trade-offs considered:
- LRU vs lease: LRU is simple but expensive to maintain under high concurrency; leases move cost off critical path and provide explicit ownership semantics at the cost of additional metadata.
- Lease duration: long leases simplify correctness but increase memory residency; borrowable short leases minimize residency but require precise drain detection.
- Cohort granularity: coarse cohorts lower churn but risk keeping cold prefixes longer. We will initially use 4 cohorts based on token-length quartiles and adjust via telemetry.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- No KV-use-after-free observed across 1000x chaos runs with continuous batching at 4x production QPS.
- 95th percentile latency degradation <= 5% for standard gen request mix when borrowable leases are enabled versus baseline.
- GPU memory fragmentation (measured by wasted bytes per-GPU) reduced by >= 20% at steady state compared to current TTL-only baseline.
- Rollout toggle present: feature flag with canary targeting 10% of traffic and automatic rollback on error budget exceed.

Testing & verification plan:
- Unit tests: borrow increment/decrement, fence install/uninstall, cohort rebalance invariants.
- Integration tests: multi-worker harness that simulates continuous batching; assert no reads to reclaimed addresses via canary checks.
- Chaos and stress: run 72-hour soak in staging with randomized borrow durations, simulated node reboots, and network partitions; run deterministic replay from recorded traces.
- Formal invariant tests: model checker script (spin-style) to verify safety property for small state-space (n<=3 workers, m<=4 prefixes).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: Feature gated binary with unit/integration tests (internal only).
- Phase 1: Canary on non-critical stack (10% traffic) + increased telemetry.
- Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 50% with performance experiments and cohort tuning.
- Phase 3: Global rollout + document recommended cohort profiles for common workloads.

Rollback strategy: Turn off borrowing (fall back to conservative TTL with admission throttles); fencing is idempotent and safe to disable. A fast rollback flag is required in the control plane.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Precise borrow counter representation under RDMA-style transfers between nodes.
- Interaction with persistent KV snapshotting for Private deployments (on-disk lease persistence semantics).
- How to surface borrow-counters and fences in Console for observability (trace events vs counters).
